text.p: The Lebanese pound continued to rise against the dollar in a quiet market in the week ended on Friday, dealers said.

The Bank of Lebanon lowered its bid-offer intervention band during the week to 1,536.50-1,546 pounds per dollar from 1,537-1,546.5 and the dollar traded at the bottom of the band throughout the week, dealers said.
"The market was quiet. The dollar was over-supplied this week but supply was a little bit less on Friday," a dealer told Reuters.
The dollar was restricted to a tight range of up to 35 piastres at the bid end of the intervention band, putting it at 1,536.50-1,536.70, he said. Most trade was at 1,536.70.
Last week the dollar closed at 1,537.35 pound in interbank trading.
